algorithm: The new algorithm derives eight scalar features by combining anisotropic regional moments, gradient-energy concentrations, vertical intensity contrast, and a centroid-shift asymmetry measure, all computed with deterministic NumPy operations.
code:
import numpy as np

def extract_features(image: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    image = np.asarray(image, dtype=float)
    h, w = image.shape

    # Regional split into quadrants
    half_h, half_w = h // 2, w // 2
    q_tl = image[:half_h, :half_w]
    q_tr = image[:half_h, half_w:]
    q_bl = image[half_h:, :half_w]
    q_br = image[half_h:, half_w:]

    # Gradient magnitudes in two orientations
    gx = np.abs(np.diff(image, axis=1, prepend=image[:, :1]))
    gy = np.abs(np.diff(image, axis=0, prepend=image[:1, :]))

    # Vertical intensity contrast (top vs bottom)
    top = image[:half_h, :]
    bottom = image[half_h:, :]

    # Centroid shift (mass imbalance between upper and lower halves)
    total_mass = np.sum(image)
    y_coords = np.arange(h)[:, None]
    centroid_y = np.sum(image * y_coords) / (total_mass + 1e-12)
    centroid_shift = centroid_y / h - 0.5

    # Threshold based on median
    med = np.median(image)
    thr = med + np.std(image) * 0.5

    return np.array([
        np.mean(q_tl) - np.mean(q_br),          # diagonal intensity contrast
        np.mean(q_tr) - np.mean(q_bl),          # anti-diagonal contrast
        np.std(np.concatenate([gx.ravel(), gy.ravel()])),  # gradient variability
        np.mean(gx) / (np.mean(gy) + 1e-12),   # gradient anisotropy
        np.mean(top) - np.mean(bottom),         # vertical intensity difference
        np.mean(np.abs(top - bottom)),          # absolute vertical contrast
        centroid_shift,                          # mass centroid shift
        np.mean(image > thr)                     # high-intensity proportion
    ], dtype=float)
